passages.text: Arnoseris is a monotypic genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.

The only known species is Arnoseris minima, native to Europe, Morocco, and the Middle East; naturalized in parts of northeastern North America (Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Maine, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Michigan). Common names in the United States: dwarf nipplewort or lamb-succory. Common names in the British Isles: lamb's succory.
It has a maximum height of 30 cm, is herbaceous and does not spread vegetatively.
The species became extinct across the British Isles in 1971. There was an attempt to reintroduce the species, and there has been one recent sighting in England.
Arnoseris minima is an annual weed of cornfields and fallow fields, favouring infertile, sandy, acidic soils.

The word 'succory' is an anglicization of the French 'cichorie' (chicory). The 'lamb' in the name denotes that it is a chicory only suitable for animal consumption. The genus Arnoseris comes from the Ancient Greek 'arnos seris' meaning 'sheep's endive'. The species epithet minima means 'small'.

Secondary metabolites 
Arnoseris minima is a source of the simple coumarin aesculetin and the flavonoids luteolin, luteolin 7-O-β-D-glucoside, luteolin 4'-O-β-D-glucoside, and 3-O-methylquercetin.

Herb, annual, 5-32 cm high. Flowering stems numerous, scapelike, erect, hollow above, pale green and often tinged red, pilose or glabrous, striate, branched or unbranched, branched in upper half. Rosette leaves few to many, obovate, (0.5)-1.0-9.0 cm long, 0.3-2.0 cm wide, dentate, acute to obtuse, petiole-like attenuate with a winged petiole, puberulous or scabridulous, yellowish green on both surfaces, sometimes tinged purple on upper surface. Synflorescence corymbiform, with 1-3 heads. Peduncle long, apically inflated, glabrous or pilose, without bracts. Heads with 20-50 flowers. Involucre at flowering broadly campanulate, 3.0-6.0 mm long, at flowering (4.0)-7.0-11.0 mm in diameter; involucral bracts oblong-ovate or narrowly ovate, green, glabrous or scaly, minutely ciliate; outer involucral bracts linear or linear-ovate, 1.5-3.0 mm long, c. 0.5 mm wide, acute; inner involucral bracts narrowly ovate, 5.0-6.0 mm long, 1.0-1.5 mm wide, acuminate. Receptacle flat, pitted, without scales. Corolla ligulate, 8.0-9.0 mm long, yellow or sometimes greenish when dry. Achenes obovoid in outline, slightly compressed, 1.5-2.2 mm long, smooth or transversely wrinkled, stramineous, with 8-10 ribs, with 3-5 stronger ribs. Pappus membranous.\r\rBased on: Bobrov, E. Arnoseris minima is a calciphobous annual psammophyte, presumably originating from the Iberian granit regions. Its area (Meusel & Jäger 1992: map 527a) is climatically delimited by summer minimum temperatures in the north and, being winter-green and thus frost-sensitive, by approximately the January isotherm of -2 to -4 °C in the east. The Central European occurrences are largely synanthropous as a weed of cereal crops and due to industrial agriculture and lack of natural habitats close to extirpation.
Flora-On botanical account for Arnoseris minima. Geographic scope: Portugal; habitat descriptions and native status on this site refer to Portugal, not the global native range.
